plain_english: Then the rite of consecration is told by the supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite: athābhiṣekasya vidhiḥ kathyate pārameśvaraḥ

plain_english: This rite, spoken in putraka initiation, is for guru and sadhaka too; it is entitled and endowed with knowledge of bhogya-tattva, in due order.
sanskrit_cite: yaiṣā putrakadīkṣoktā gurusādhakayorapi saivādhikāriṇī bhogyatattvayuktimatī kramāt

plain_english: Having known him to be a well-practiced knower, a being desiring to become a future one, and fit, the guru should confer his own authority to him.
sanskrit_cite: svabhyastajñāninaṃ santaṃ bubhūṣumatha bhāvinam yogyaṃ jñātvā svādhikāraṃ gurustasmai samarpayet

plain_english: Whoever does not know thus is not even consecrated; the teacher is set out by the order of samaya and the rest, as said in the glorious Kāmika.
sanskrit_cite: yo naivaṃ veda naivāsāvabhiṣikto@pi daiśikaḥ samayyādikrameṇeti śrīmatkāmika ucyate

plain_english: He who does not know the sixfold path-union, situated externally and internally, is not a guru who releases, according to the Siddhayogīśvarīmata.
sanskrit_cite: yo na vedādhvasandhānaṃ ṣoḍhā bāhyāntarasthitam sa gururmocayenneti siddhayogīśvarīmate

plain_english: Even one who lacks all marks, if he possesses knowledge, is regarded as a guru; thus knowledge-primacy is indeed stated in Sri Kacabhargava.
sanskrit_cite: sarvalakṣaṇahīno@pi jñānavān gururiṣyate jñānaprādhānyamevoktamiti śrīkacabhārgave

plain_english: The guru knows words, sentences, and valid means of knowledge; is solely devoted to Shiva; understands the meaning of all Shiva scriptures; and is compassionate.
sanskrit_cite: padavākyapramāṇajñaḥ śivabhaktyekatatparaḥ samastaśivaśāstrārthaboddhā kāruṇiko guruḥ

plain_english: The Supreme Lord himself states the characteristic of the self-born: the non-devotee whose thought is fixed on mere living, though he acts under Īśāna's control, is not (self-born).
sanskrit_cite: na svayaṃbhūstasya coktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ parameśinā abhakto jīvitadhiyā kurvannīśānadhiṣṭhitaḥ

plain_english: One born from a later self is self-born but not entitled; nor is the mere "sprout of ash" entitled anywhere, nor the son of a vow-keeper, nor likewise the son of bad character.
sanskrit_cite: paścātmanā svayaṃbhūṣṇurnādhikārī sa kutracit bhasmāṅkuro vratisuto duḥśīlātanayastathā

plain_english: Kuṇḍa and gola are wicked; this is said in the Devyākhyayāmala; and one reborn with another gender is again established in Śaiva.
sanskrit_cite: kuṇḍo golaśca te duṣṭā uktaṃ devyākhyayāmale punarbhūścānyaliṅgo yaḥ punaḥ śaive pratiṣṭhitaḥ

plain_english: In the Śrīpūrvaśāstra no such rule is stated; one who knows the true reality assembly is thus a revealer to the disciple.
sanskrit_cite: śrīpūrvaśāstre na tveṣa niyamaḥ ko@pi coditaḥ yathārthatattvasaṃghajñastathā śiṣye prakāśakaḥ

plain_english: Again, one who knows all principles and the like, and the characteristic in Yogacara, should practice wherever in tantra it is taught, as it is taught.
sanskrit_cite: yaḥ punaḥ sarvatattvāni vettītyādi ca lakṣaṇam yogacāre ca yadyatra tantre coditamācaret

plain_english: Thus indeed, for success, this command is declared; but there, the ritual teacher excludes one-eyed and similar persons.
sanskrit_cite: tathaiva siddhaye seyamājñeti kila varṇitam yastu karmitayācāryastatra kāṇādivarjanam

plain_english: Because action is nowhere greater than the completeness of the agent; and in the Devi Yamala scripture there is avoidance of Kanci and similar places.
sanskrit_cite: yataḥ kārakasāmagryātkarmaṇo nādhikaḥ kvacit devyā yāmalaśāstre ca kāñcyādiparivarjanam

plain_english: Since faults such as anger are seen, how can that be in a well-knowing teacher? But teachers such as Svayambhu and others are to be avoided in the Yamala and similar texts.
sanskrit_cite: taddṛṣṭadoṣātkrodhādeḥ samyakjñātaryasau kutaḥ guravastu svayaṃbhvādi varjyaṃ yadyāmalādiṣu

plain_english: They explained all that by ritual intent; therefore there is the conception of place, family, conduct, and bodily marks.
sanskrit_cite: karmyabhiprāyataḥ sarvaṃ taditi vyācacakṣire ato deśakulācāradehalakṣaṇakalpanām

plain_english: Disregarding all else, the guru should make the disciple a guru: having worshipped as before and offered oblation, he causes him to hear the intended matter.
sanskrit_cite: anādṛtyaiva saṃpūrṇajñānaṃ kuryādgururgurum prāgvatsaṃpūjya hutvā ca śrāvayitvā cikīrṣitam

plain_english: Then the guru consecrates the disciple with sixty-four; then, once, with that mantra-essence water, by the previously stated rite.
sanskrit_cite: tato@bhiṣiñcettaṃ śiṣyaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā tataḥ sakṛt tanmantrarasatoyena pūrvoktavidhinā guruḥ

plain_english: Then, by abundance and in a well-spread way, he would tell him his own all duty-essence, the supreme secret of the scriptures.
sanskrit_cite: vibhavena suvistīrṇaṃ tatastasmai vadetsvakam sarvaṃ kartavyasāraṃ yacchāstrāṇāṃ paramaṃ rahaḥ

plain_english: The disciples you should favor are those impelled by Shiva-Shakti; this was stated in the Jnanottara; and these are Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas.
sanskrit_cite: anugrāhyāstvayā śiṣyāḥ śivaśaktipracoditāḥ uktaṃ jñānottare caitadbrāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā viśaḥ

plain_english: Eunuchs, women, śūdras, and others who desire that are not to be examined in initiation; they should be examined at the time of knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: napuṃsakāḥ striyaḥ śūdrā ye cānye@pi tadarthinaḥ te dīkṣāyāṃ na mīmāṃsyā jñānakāle vicārayet

plain_english: The teacher, rooted in knowledge, is declared to conduct the seven-sacrifice: initiation, explanation, compassion, friendship, reflection on scripture, and unity with Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: jñānamūlo guruḥ proktaḥ saptasatrīṃ pravartayet dīkṣā vyākhyā kṛpā maitrī śāstracintā śivaikatā

plain_english: In the consecration rite, food-giving and related offerings sustain the seven-sacrifice, and karaṇī, khaṭikā, and related items are given to him.
sanskrit_cite: annādidānamityetatpālayetsaptasatrakam abhiṣekavidhau cāsmai karaṇīkhaṭikādikam

plain_english: All the throng of equipment is to be offered to the wise one; the one consecrated should afterwards honor the teacher with gifts.
sanskrit_cite: sarvopakaraṇavrātamarpaṇīyaṃ vipaścite so@bhiṣikto guruṃ paścāddakṣiṇābhiḥ prapūjayet

plain_english: A teacher without knowledge, having handed over his own authority to a ritual worker, should not perform initiation and authority without doing so again by his command.
sanskrit_cite: jñānahīno guruḥ karmī svādhikāraṃ samarpya no dīkṣādyadhikṛtiṃ kuryādvinā tasyājñayā punaḥ

plain_english: Thus he should make him hear; even he should bow and greet. Then from that point on, the former teacher is one who has relinquished authority.
sanskrit_cite: ityevaṃ śrāvayetso@pi namaskṛtyābhinandayet tataḥ prabhṛtyasau pūrvo gurustyaktādhikārakaḥ

plain_english: As he wishes, he may move about in teaching, initiation, and related matters, free from restraint; he is not hindered in acting, because such transmission is like one lamp from another.
sanskrit_cite: yathecchaṃ vicaredvyākhyādīkṣādau yantraṇojjhitaḥ kurvanna bādhyate yasmāddīpāddīpavadīdṛśaḥ

plain_english: In the Siddhanta tantra it is said that the lineage of non-authority is hindered: falling while acting, and before that, acting itself would be hindered.
sanskrit_cite: santāno nādhikārasya cyavo@kurvanna bādhyate prāk ca kurvanvihanyeta siddhātantre taducyate

plain_english: But a teacher who gives instruction according to its meaning is not called contemptuous toward liberation from saṃsāra at the time of the rite.
sanskrit_cite: yathārthamupadeśaṃ tu kurvannācārya ucyate na cāvajñā kriyākāle saṃsāroddharaṇaṃ prati

plain_english: A guru endowed with truth should not initiate a disciple out of pride; one who does so would dwell in hell and become diseased in this life.
sanskrit_cite: na dīkṣeta guruḥ śiṣyaṃ tattvayuktastu garvataḥ yo@sya syānnarake vāsa iha ca vyādhito bhavet

plain_english: Having received consecration, that guru should for six months meditate upon and recite all the mantra-methods taught in the tantras, from oneness.
sanskrit_cite: prāptābhiṣekaḥ sa guruḥ ṣaṇmāsānmantrapaddhatim sarvāṃ tantroditāṃ dhyāyejjapeccātanmayatvataḥ

plain_english: When one has truly become one with that, power is attained; then bonds are to be cut, and effort must be made to remain established in that identification.
sanskrit_cite: yadaiva tanmayībhūtastadā vīryamupāgataḥ chindyātpāśāṃstato yatnaṃ kuryāttanmayatāsthitau

plain_english: A subtle line, like moon-crystal, rises from the heart cakra; it is sound-form, tranquil, and goes through the row of cakras.
sanskrit_cite: hṛccakrādutthitā sūkṣmā śaśisphaṭikasaṃnibhā lekhākārā nādarūpā praśāntā cakrapaṅktigā

plain_english: Rooted at the twelfth end, that [form] lies in the suṣumnā between the three paths; there, having filled the heart cakra, one should mutter the blazing-bright mantra.
sanskrit_cite: dvādaśānte nirūḍhā sā sauṣumne tripathāntare tatra hṛccakramāpūrya japenmantraṃ jvalatprabham

plain_english: It resembles a thighlike flood of flame issuing through the holes of eyes and hair, scattered up to a quiet flame-tip, dissolving all ghee.
sanskrit_cite: cakṣurlomādirandhraughavahajjvālaurvasaṃnibham yāvacchāntaśikhākīrṇaṃ viśvājyapravilāpakam

plain_english: When the mind's inner space is satiated by a stream of ghee, mantras thus become givers of liberation; they would be radiant, awakened, and very pure.
sanskrit_cite: tadājyadhārāsaṃtṛptamānābhikuharāntaram evaṃ mantrā mokṣadāḥ syurdīptā buddhāḥ sunirmalāḥ

plain_english: It goes through the root, bulb, navel, heart, throat, and palate; through the half-moon, the end of sound, and the pervading power.
sanskrit_cite: mūlakandanabhonābhihṛtkaṇṭhālikatālugam ardhendurodhikānādatadantavyāpiśaktigam

plain_english: Where, in the circle of muttering, resting in the pure self and other circle, from all scattered distinction.
sanskrit_cite: samanonmanaśuddhātmaparacakrasamāśritam yatra yatra japeccakre samastavyastabhedanāt

plain_english: There, in the Tantra named after the Goddess, this vidyā-vow—called the great mantra—is declared for the accomplishment of mantra potency.
sanskrit_cite: tatra tatra mahāmantra iti devyākhyayāmale vidyāvratamidaṃ proktaṃ mantravīryaprasiddhaye

plain_english: And that identity-only, as stated in the Spanda treatise, having overcome power, the mantras are of the all-knowing, power-possessing one.
sanskrit_cite: tacca tādātmyameveti yaduktaṃ spandaśāsane tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ

plain_english: Having completed the vow of knowledge, after initiation, explanation, and the like, in every way, they proceed for authority, like the instruments of embodied beings.
sanskrit_cite: pravartante@dhikārāya karaṇānīva dehinām kṛtavidyāvrataḥ paścāddīkṣāvyākhyādi sarvataḥ

plain_english: He should do this among fit disciples, never among unfit ones; in secret he should join a brahmin, having tested him contrariwise.
sanskrit_cite: kuryādyogyeṣu śiṣyeṣu nāyogyeṣu kadācana rahasye yojayedvipraṃ parīkṣya viparītataḥ

plain_english: Power comes from conduct, not otherwise, according to the ūrmi teaching; the small daily practices should be performed as stated in the Brahmayāmala.
sanskrit_cite: ācārācchaktimapyeva nānyathetyūrmiśāsane nityādyalpālpakaṃ kuryādyaduktaṃ brahmayāmale

plain_english: O dear, one who has completed the knowledge-vow remembers all by mind; but one whose all-knowing is concealed by bodily connection is a vessel of hypocrisy.
sanskrit_cite: cīrṇavidyāvrataḥ sarvaṃ manasā vā smaretpriye dehasaṃbandhasaṃchannasārvajñyo dambhabhājanam

plain_english: Even if he does not initiate, the teacher is never defiled; having recognized his unfitness, he would not initiate him, in order to avoid harm.
sanskrit_cite: avidandīkṣamāṇo@pi na duṣyeddaiśikaḥ kvacit jñātvā tvayogyatāṃ nainaṃ dīkṣeta pratyavāyitām

plain_english: Having known him in knowledge, scripture, attainment, guru-ness, and so on, one should examine him again and again to see whether he possesses fitness for each [relevant qualification].
sanskrit_cite: buddhvā jñāne śāstrasiddhigurutvādau ca taṃ punaḥ bhūya eva parīkṣeta tattadaucityaśālinam

plain_english: There one should appoint, never by reversal; for surely, whence arises desire for that unfit thing?
sanskrit_cite: tatra tatra niyuñjīta natu jātu viparyayāt nanu tadvastvayogyasya tatrecchā jāyate kutaḥ

plain_english: A desire empowered by that Lord indeed indicates his fitness; truly, some awakened desire does not attain establishment.
sanskrit_cite: tadīśādhiṣṭhitecchaiva yogyatāmasya sūcayet satyaṃ kāpi prabuddhāsāvicchā rūḍhiṃ na gacchati

plain_english: Just as a lightning-like sinful nature is abandoned, with rooted and unrooted states, so too that desire arises by Shambhu's grace.
sanskrit_cite: vidyudvatpāpaśīlasya yathā pāpāpavarjane rūḍhyarūḍhī tadicchāyā api śaṃbhuprasādataḥ

plain_english: Only one whose desire has not taken root is not a vessel for it; and one who, though possessing right knowledge, lacks faith in the guru.
sanskrit_cite: aprarūḍhatathecchākastata eva na bhājanam yaḥ samyagjñānamādāya guruviśvāsavarjitaḥ

plain_english: If this is known here, the world would not be destroyed; knowledge should be bestowed; even if it is unknown, when it is known again, one should practice the removal of knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: lokaṃ viplāvayennāsmiñjñāte vijñānamarpayet ajñāte@pi punarjñāte vijñānaharaṇaṃ caret

plain_english: When it is known again and again yet lacks trust, then one should meditate before him, throbbing like the moon and sun.
sanskrit_cite: punaḥpunaryadā jñāto viśvāsaparivarjitaḥ tadā tamagrato dhyāyetsphurantaṃ candrasūryavat

plain_english: Then one should meditate on the deluding left power, which rises from the sky of wisdom of one's own heart-lotus and is darkened by Rahu.
sanskrit_cite: tato nijahṛdambhojabodhāmbarataloditām svarbhānumalināṃ dhyāyedvāmāṃ śaktiṃ vimohanīm

plain_english: Having contemplated her as having emerged by the left-hand procedure and as proceeding toward the goal, one should contemplate him as light swallowed by her.
sanskrit_cite: vāmācārakrameṇaināṃ niḥsṛtāṃ sādhyagāminīm cintayitvā tayā grastaprakāśaṃ taṃ vicintayet

plain_english: By this sequence-yoga, for one of deluded mind and evil soul, knowledge, mantra, science, and the like cause harm.
sanskrit_cite: anena kramayogena mūḍhabuddherdurātmanaḥ vijñānamantravidyādyāḥ prakurvantyapakāritām

plain_english: But how could knowledge situated in the self be taken away? Therefore how is knowledge-removal said to be preceded by śrī?
sanskrit_cite: nanu vijñānamātmasthaṃ kathaṃ hartuṃ kṣamaṃ bhavet ato vijñānaharaṇaṃ kathaṃ śrīpūrva ucyate

plain_english: It is said: since the disciple's knowledge has fully matured, why should it be removed from one who possesses complete fitness?
sanskrit_cite: ucyate nāsya śiṣyasya vijñānaṃ rūḍhimāgatam tathātve haraṇaṃ kasmātpūrṇayogyatvaśālinaḥ

plain_english: But this fool is deeply made by the Lord's Vāmā power by nature alone; therefore his vidyā and the rest are harmful.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃtveṣa vāmayā śaktyā mūḍho gāḍhaṃ vibhoḥ kṛtaḥ svabhāvādeva tenāsya vidyādyamapakārakam

plain_english: Again, the teacher is identical with Shiva; if the consecrated one performs the fivefold action, then his full authority is that.
sanskrit_cite: guruḥ punaḥ śivābhinnaḥ sanyaḥ pañcavidhāṃ kṛtim kuryādyadi tataḥ pūrṇamadhikāritvamasya tat

plain_english: So the guru is authorized over the fourfold task — creation and maintenance of the pure realities, their impurity and their dissolution — through the joining (of the paths) and grace.
sanskrit_cite: ato yathā śuddhatattvasṛṣṭisthityormalātyaye yojanānugrahe kāryacatuṣke@dhikṛto guruḥ

plain_english: By non-difference from Shiva, he performs that; like the fifth, this too is the duty called disappearance; thus that one is of Shiva-nature.
sanskrit_cite: śivābhedena tatkuryāttadvatpañcamamapyayam tirobhāvābhidhaṃ kṛtyaṃ tathāsau śivatātmakaḥ

plain_english: Therefore, indeed, in Shiva, in scripture, in knowledge, and in the vessel of reassurance, even the abode of anger is not hidden by the guru's foolishness.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva śive śāstre jñāne cāśvāsabhājanam gurormūḍhatayā kopadhāmāpi na tirohitaḥ

plain_english: Indeed, one whose teacher is angered is called hidden, a worldly being; yet he is God indeed—not a teacher, nor a false knower.
sanskrit_cite: gururhi kupito yasya sa tirohita ucyate saṃsārī satu devo hi gururna ca mṛṣāvidaḥ

plain_english: Therefore, although the defamer of scriptures and the like is not burned by the angry guru, yet he is obscured.
sanskrit_cite: tata eva ca śāstrādidūṣako yadyapi krudhā na dahyate@sau guruṇā tathāpyeṣa tirohitaḥ

plain_english: This is the coming of our teacher: when he is hidden in a child, one should not be angry, nor should the wise one curse, for he is indeed always a benefactor.
sanskrit_cite: asmadgurvāgamastveṣa tirobhūte svayaṃ śiśau na kupyenna śapeddhīmān sa hyanugrāhakaḥ sadā

plain_english: If, impelled by the Lord's will, he strangles the bond in his throat, what is the teacher to do for him there? Would there be cooperation?
sanskrit_cite: īśecchācoditaḥ pāśaṃ yadi kaṇṭhe nipīḍayet kimācāryeṇa tatrāsya kāryā syātsahakāritā

plain_english: Even though the guru is non-different from Shiva, he is indeed the Lord's principal, grace-filled power; one devoted to that power should be graced by him in every way.
sanskrit_cite: śivābhinno@pi hi gururanugrahamayīṃ vibhoḥ mukhyāṃ śaktimupāsīno@nugṛhṇīyātsa sarvathā

plain_english: But scripture is spoken only to awaken awareness of freedom; it is not an action to perform. For those who are falling, a hand-support is acceptable, but making them fall is not.
sanskrit_cite: svātantryamātrajñaptyai tu kathitaṃ śāstra īdṛśam na kāryaṃ patatāṃ hastālambaḥ sahyo na pātanam

plain_english: Therefore, having purified him with expiations, the guru should initiate him with compassion, since he is again facing the desire for independence and the like.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva svatantratvādicchāyāḥ punarunmukham prāyaścittairviśodhyainaṃ dīkṣeta kṛpayā guruḥ

plain_english: Approaching with an upward gaze and then being well reassured, one approaches the supreme; even by approaching the lower scripture, one may not attain worthiness of good.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhvadṛṣṭau prapannaḥ sannanāśvastastataḥ param adhaḥśāstraṃ prapadyāpi na śreyaḥpātratāmiyāt

plain_english: One fallen into downward vision, whose mind is not reassured by it, yet holding the upward command: sin; let him abandon that and become Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: adhodṛṣṭau prapannastu tadanāśvastamānasaḥ ūrdhvaśāsanabhāk pāpaṃ taccojjhecca śivībhavet

plain_english: Even a minister, though a limb of the king, is ruined if he harms the king; but the reversal is not the same—one should resort to the upward view.
sanskrit_cite: rājñe druhyannamātyāṅgabhūto@pi hi vihanyate viparyayastu netyevamūrdhvāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ samāśrayet

plain_english: In the earlier Śrī-śāstra it was stated by him: as long as it is not extracted by him alone, here the meaning is this much, augmented by prior knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ yāvattenaiva noddhṛtaḥ atra hyartho@yametāvatpūrvoktajñānavṛṃhitaḥ

plain_english: Thus here the guru is indeed the one referred to by that word: one who possesses such practiced knowledge and holds high status.
sanskrit_cite: gurustāvatsa evātra tacchabdenāvamṛśyate tādṛksvabhyastavijñānabhājordhvapadaśālinā

plain_english: One who has not been uplifted has no welfare; welfare arises through upliftment by the guru, whether this one or another. Therefore the example of the lotus-born and the sun is explained here.
sanskrit_cite: anuddhṛtasya na śreya etadanyagurūddhṛteḥ ata evāmbujanmārkadṛṣṭānto@tra nirūpitaḥ

plain_english: The light of the three worlds is one; indeed another light is night-made; knowledge is another for the Trika guru, and another for those dwelling in your nature.
sanskrit_cite: trijagajjyotiṣo hyanyattejo@nyacca niśākṛtaḥ jñānamanyattrikaguroranyattvadharavartinām

plain_english: Therefore, when one is in the state of a former guru, then one should again resort to that other who is endowed with marks, facing upward.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva purābhūtagurvabhāvo yadā tadā tadanyaṃ lakṣaṇopetamāśrayetpunarunmukhaḥ

plain_english: If that state is present, the upward-facing one should not abandon it out of doubt; clearly, doing so would be a fault—one of two possible courses—that destroys authority.
sanskrit_cite: sati tasmiṃstūnmukhaḥ sankasmājjahyādyadi sphuṭam syādanyatarago doṣo yo@dhikārāpaghātakaḥ

plain_english: Here the fault is not determined as a fault simply because it stands in the world; rather, that one is considered to be of a nature connected with explaining ignorance.
sanskrit_cite: doṣaśceha na lokastho doṣatvena nirūpyate ajñānakhyāpanāyuktakhyāpanātmā tvasau mataḥ

plain_english: Even for the disciple, the chief fault is the unsteady form of such knowledge; other faults arise from it.
sanskrit_cite: śiṣyasyāpi tathābhūtajñānānāśvastarūpatā mukhyo doṣastadanye hi doṣāstatprabhavā yataḥ

plain_english: Who indeed greatly esteems a physician when disease is already destroyed? Surely an envious one, whose disease is destroyed, becomes healthy by force.
sanskrit_cite: na dhvastavyādhikaḥ ko hi bhiṣajaṃ bahu manyate asūyurnūnamadhvastavyādhiḥ svasthāyate balāt

plain_english: Thus, one comforted by knowledge—what should he not do for the guru? If not indeed untrusted, he stands like one trusted.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ jñānasamāśvastaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na gurave caret no cennūnamaviśvasto viśvasta iva tiṣṭhati

plain_english: In the Mālinīvijayottara it is said that the faults beginning with ignorance belonging to the guru are not worldly faults, in order to declare this.
sanskrit_cite: ajñānādaya evaite doṣā na laukikā guroḥ iti khyāpayituṃ proktaṃ mālinīvijayottare

plain_english: One should not investigate his conduct, whether auspicious or inauspicious; he himself knows whether it is proper or improper.
sanskrit_cite: na tasyānveṣayedvṛttaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham sa eva tadvijānāti yuktaṃ cāyuktameva vā

plain_english: When someone is attached to forbidden things that steal life and wealth, that person should be restrained by a humble wise one.
sanskrit_cite: akāryeṣu yadā saktaḥ prāṇadravyāpahāriṣu tadā nivāraṇīyo@sau praṇatena vipaścitā

plain_english: A forbidden act is defined by its stated intention; even if someone is strongly restrained by another, if he does not turn back, the matter remains unresolved in the supplied fragment.
sanskrit_cite: viśeṣaṇamakāryāṇāmuktābhiprāyameva yat tenātivāryamāṇo@pi yadyasau na nivartate

plain_english: Then, having gone elsewhere, one should meditate on Śiva alone; indeed there is no fault in his guru-hood by which one would farm a barren field.
sanskrit_cite: tadānyatra kvacidgatvā śivamevānucintayet na hyasya sa gurutve syāddoṣo yenoṣare kṛṣim

plain_english: At night one should act or go; or he, a thief of wealth and life, fearing his displeasure, should then behave in that way.
sanskrit_cite: kuryādvrajenniśāyāṃ vā sa tvarthaprāṇahārakaḥ tadīyāpriyabhīrustu paraṃ tādṛśamācaret

plain_english: Because it is unpleasant, he will not hear what is spoken; in Śrīmātaṅga it is said, and it is not studied out of fear of the earth.
sanskrit_cite: yatastadapriyaṃ naiṣa śṛṇuyāditi bhāṣitam śrīmātaṅge taduktaṃ ca nādhītaṃ bhūmabhītitaḥ

plain_english: What is said as 'this much is to be done' is firm; for those seized by intense power, it shines by itself in the heart.
sanskrit_cite: yaccaitaduktametāvatkartavyamiti taddhruvam tīvraśaktigṛhītānāṃ svayameva hṛdi sphuret

plain_english: This teaching is declared to gradually kindle one's own power for those of weak or medium capacity; that power then blazes sufficiently.
sanskrit_cite: upadeśastvayaṃ mandamadhyaśakternijāṃ kramāt śaktiṃ jvalayituṃ proktaḥ sā hyevaṃ jājvalītyalam

plain_english: Those who partake in the abundance of beautiful ardor born of firm attachment are self-exultant; love is all; firmness elsewhere is seen.
sanskrit_cite: dṛḍhānurāgasubhagasaṃrambhābhogabhāginaḥ svollāsi smarasarvasyaṃ dārḍhyāyānyatra dṛśyate

plain_english: Indeed, why is this an example? What inauspicious thing has been done by it? Consciousness-pulsation is all-pervading; from a different substrate, he is thus, thus.
sanskrit_cite: nanveṣa kasmāddṛṣṭāntaḥ kimetenāśubhaṃ kṛtam citspandaḥ sarvago bhinnādupādheḥ sa tathā tathā

plain_english: Even one who is hidden and again becomes manifest is liberated by himself, even without a teacher.
sanskrit_cite: bhavetko@pi tirobhūtaḥ punarunmukhito@pi san vināpi daiśikātprāgvatsvayameva vimucyate

plain_english: This manner is not stated here; it arises from the strength of śaktipāta; and here, by impossibility, it is like firm anger and favor.
sanskrit_cite: prakārastveṣa nātroktaḥ śaktipātabalādgataḥ asaṃbhāvyatayā cātra dṛḍhakopaprasādavat

plain_english: Thus this rule declared by the teacher: the teacher should protect it; otherwise he would not attain auspiciousness in the glorious essence, as described.
sanskrit_cite: ityeṣa yo guroḥ prokto vidhistaṃ pālayedguruḥ anyathā na śivaṃ yāyācchrīmatsāre ca varṇitam

plain_english: Those teachers who wrongly carry out the scriptural meaning and sufficiently abandon it, dwelling in Ardhanārīśapura, are fallen from the vow.
sanskrit_cite: anyāyaṃ ye prakurvanti śāstrārthaṃ varjayantyalam te@rdhanārīśapuragā guravaḥ samayacyutāḥ

plain_english: Elsewhere too there is authority, which would lead to lordship of vidyā; elsewhere, by abandoning the vow, one becomes a flesh-eater for a hundred years.
sanskrit_cite: anyatrāpyadhikāraṃ ca neyādvidyeśatāṃ vrajet anyatra samayatyāgātkravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ

plain_english: Such is the meaning there; the Siddhanta guru's conclusion is that one becomes lord of piśāca-vidyā, but the tantric is indeed pure.
sanskrit_cite: iyattatratyatātparyaṃ siddhāntagururunnayaḥ bhavetpiśācavidyeśaḥ śuddha eva tu tāntrikaḥ

plain_english: This is called the path of teachers for whom karma predominates: the station or world of the six-half-teacher and ardhanari.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaḍardhadaiśikaścārdhanārīśabhuvanasthitiḥ eṣā karmapradhānānāṃ gurūṇāṃ gatirucyate

plain_english: For knowers, this is not bondage; thus it is stated everywhere. Even in the adept's consecration, all this rite is said.
sanskrit_cite: jñānināṃ caiṣa no bandha iti sarvatra varṇitam sādhakasyābhiṣeke@pi sarvo@yaṃ kathyate vidhiḥ

plain_english: Here there is no conferral of authority and no knowledge-vow; rather, an accomplishable mantra is conferred within one's own useful sequence of rites.
sanskrit_cite: adhikārārpaṇaṃ nātra naca vidyāvrataṃ kila sādhyamantrārpaṇaṃ tvatra svopayogikriyākrame

plain_english: In the complete teaching, one should offer one's own implements; the consecration rite is determined by the Supreme Lord, as it has been determined.
sanskrit_cite: samaste@pyupadeśaḥ syānnijopakaraṇārpaṇam abhiṣekavidhirnirūpitaḥ parameśena yathā nirūpitaḥ
